summary: order-service p99 blew up from ~150ms to ~5.3s with ledger-db statement timeouts on INSERT INTO orders starting 09:00:42Z. The fault is NOT in order-service (no release this week) nor the DBA autovacuum change. Root cause is portfolio-service deploy dep-5905 (v4.5.0, live at 08:56:00Z) which added an unindexed query 'SELECT * FROM trades WHERE account_id=$1 AND executed_at > $2 ORDER BY executed_at'; the planner does a Seq Scan over 48.2M trades rows, driving shared ledger-db CPU 30%->96%, slow queries ~1->140/min and connections 62->190. order-service, a co-tenant of ledger-db, then blocks on its INSERTs and times out. Autovacuum cfg-2903 (08:00Z) is ruled out because metrics stayed flat for ~45 min after it and only moved with the 08:56 deploy; payment/settlement are unaffected, ruling out a global DB infrastructure fault. Recommended: roll back dep-5905 or add a composite index on trades(account_id, executed_at) immediately.

ranked_hypotheses.title: portfolio-service deploy introduced an unindexed seq-scan query that saturated shared ledger-db
ranked_hypotheses.statement: portfolio-service v4.5.0 (dep-5905, 08:56Z) added a query 'SELECT * FROM trades WHERE account_id=$1 AND executed_at > $2 ORDER BY executed_at' with no supporting index and no migration. The planner does a Seq Scan over 48.2M trades rows for every call, driving ledger-db CPU 30%->96%, slow queries ~1->140/min and connections 62->190. order-service INSERTs against the same shared DB then queue and hit their statement timeout, producing the reported p99>5s and order timeouts.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5905 deploys a new unindexed trades query at 08:56Z
query does Seq Scan on 48.2M-row trades table, 1-9s per call
ledger-db CPU/slow-queries/connections spike (08:45 bucket onward, sustained from 09:00)
order-service shares ledger-db and its INSERTs block -> order-service p99 150ms->5.3s, pool 14->46
order-service INSERT INTO orders statement timeouts begin 09:00:42Z

assumptions: The new portfolio query is executed at high volume (e.g. per user/page) rather than as a one-off report
order-service and portfolio-service share the same ledger-db instance/cluster (implied by the shared datastore edge)

ranked_hypotheses.title: DBA autovacuum config change caused ledger-db degradation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 08:00Z change cfg-2903 (autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.2->0.1, 'More aggressive autovacuum') triggered heavier vacuum activity on ledger-db, raising CPU and I/O and causing order INSERT timeouts. This is the change the reporter flagged and it is on the blamed datastore.

causal_chain.claim: increased autovacuum load raises ledger-db CPU

assumptions: Autovacuum scale-factor 0.1 could meaningfully raise resource use on this DB
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: cfg-2903 was applied at 08:00Z but ledger-db CPU was flat at ~30% and slow_queries ~1/min through the 08:30 bucket, ~45 minutes later. The degradation coincides with the 08:56 portfolio-service deploy and its 08:58:38 seq-scan query, not with cfg-2903.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Generic ledger-db infrastructure failure (disk/IOPS/storage) independent of any change
ranked_hypotheses.statement: ledger-db suffered an infrastructure-level slowdown (e.g. IOPS throttling like HIST-110) that slowed all queries and caused order timeouts.

causal_chain.claim: all queries slow, order INSERTs time out

assumptions: A platform-level storage fault could exist without a deploy
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The slowdown is attributable to a specific new query pattern (F6) and payment/settlement, which also use ledger-db, are essentially unaffected (F11); an infrastructure fault would degrade all consumers uniformly.

facts.statement: ledger-db is a shared postgres used by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service.
order-service produced 284 ledger-db statement-timeout errors on INSERT INTO orders, first at 09:00:42Z.
order-service p99 latency rose from ~150ms to ~5300ms with onset in the 08:45 bucket.
order-service db_pool_in_use rose from ~14 to ~46 connections.
portfolio-service v4.5.0 (dep-5905) deployed at 08:56:00Z with a new unindexed query on trades and no migration; still live.
ledger-db logged the new portfolio-service query doing a Seq Scan on 48,211,907 rows, 1-9s per call, from 08:58:38Z.
ledger-db CPU rose from ~30% to ~96% starting in the 08:45 bucket.
ledger-db slow_queries_per_min rose from ~1 to ~140 starting in the 08:45 bucket.
ledger-db connections_active rose from ~62 to ~190 starting in the 08:45 bucket.
The only config change was ledger-db autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.2->0.1 at 08:00:00Z.
payment-service (0 warnings) and settlement-service (1 warning) were essentially unaffected despite sharing ledger-db.
HIST-111 was a past bad_deployment of the same shape: an unindexed report query doing full scans on ledger-db.

timeline.event: DBA config change cfg-2903: ledger-db autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.2->0.1 (no metric effect for ~45 min).
ledger-db CPU/slow-queries/connections begin rising; order-service p99 bucket avg jumps to 512ms.
portfolio-service v4.5.0 (dep-5905) deployed with new unindexed trades query.
First ledger-db slow query log: 8690ms seq scan on trades, application_name=portfolio-service.
ledger-db CPU ~96%, ~140 slow queries/min, ~190 connections; order-service p99 ~5300ms and pool ~46.
First order-service statement timeout on INSERT INTO orders.
Incident reported (order-service p99 > 5s, ledger-db statement timeouts).

recommended_actions.action: Roll back portfolio-service dep-5905 (v4.5.0) to the previous version to immediately stop the seq-scan load on ledger-db.
recommended_actions.rationale: The deploy introduced the unindexed query that is saturating shared ledger-db; removing it should restore order-service latency.

recommended_actions.action: Add a composite index on trades(account_id, executed_at) and verify the planner uses it (no Seq Scan on 48.2M rows).
recommended_actions.rationale: Directly removes the seq scan even if the feature is kept; mirrors HIST-111 resolution.

recommended_actions.action: Add a pre-deploy query-review/EXPLAIN gate for ledger-db-bound queries so unindexed full scans cannot reach production.
recommended_actions.rationale: HIST-111 already recommended a query review gate and this recurred.

recommended_actions.action: Add per-application DB load attribution and alerting on ledger-db CPU/slow_queries/connections so a single tenant's query regression is caught before it starves co-tenants.
recommended_actions.rationale: order-service was the reported victim but portfolio-service was the source; tenant-attribution would shorten detection.

recommended_actions.action: Do not treat/roll back cfg-2903 as the cause; keep the autovacuum change but monitor it separately.
recommended_actions.rationale: Metrics were flat for ~45 min after cfg-2903 and only moved with the 08:56 deploy, so it is not the trigger.

data_gaps: No per-application or per-query breakdown beyond application_name in slow-query logs; could not measure portfolio-service's query volume (calls/min) to quantify the load it injected.
No ledger-db disk_used_pct/replication_lag_ms inspected, so an independent storage-layer contribution cannot be fully excluded (though payment/settlement being clean argues against it).
portfolio-service call rate / request_rate metric not queried, so it is assumed the new query runs at high volume rather than rarely.
Could not confirm whether an index on trades(account_id, executed_at) ever existed or was dropped; the deploy says 'no migration included'.

findings.statement: order-service is not the only ledger-db consumer: ledger-db is a shared postgres used by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service.
order-service errors begin at 09:00:42 and are almost entirely ledger-db statement timeouts on INSERT INTO orders (284 ERROR entries).

order-service db_pool_in_use rises from ~14 to ~46 connections at the same 08:45-09:00 window, consistent with connections blocked on the DB.

findings.statement: ledger-db logs show this exact new portfolio-service query doing a Seq Scan on a 48,211,907-row trades table, taking 1-9 seconds per call; first occurrence 08:58:38Z.

findings.statement: ledger-db CPU jumps from ~30% (flat through 08:30) to a 08:45-bucket max of 96.36% and a sustained ~96% from 09:00.
ledger-db slow_queries_per_min jumps from ~1/min (through 08:30) to a 08:45-bucket max of 139.68 and a sustained ~140/min from 09:00.
ledger-db connections_active rises from ~62 to a 08:45-bucket max of 199.81 and a sustained ~190 from 09:00.
The only config change in the window is cfg-2903: ledger-db autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.2 -> 0.1 at 08:00:00Z.
Other ledger-db consumers are essentially unaffected: payment-service produced 0 WARN+ entries and settlement-service only 1 connection-reset warning in the incident window.

A past incident HIST-111 with the same shape (a new report query without an index doing full table scans on ledger-db, high DB CPU) was classified bad_deployment and resolved by adding an index plus a query review gate.
